content.statement: The cache gives back the answer it last kept for a check at a version, if it still keeps it, and keeps the newest answers, a bounded number of them.
content.why: Answers are kept by the check and its version, so a later write, which makes a new version, never meets an answer kept for an older one: staleness, the classic bug of an authorization cache, cannot happen by how the key is made (Q4). The cache is the service's own code (LruCache.scala), tested against this model on generated runs of its operations; what is decided here is the model.

lookup = fun (a : Ask) => do
    let cs ← get
    pure (match (List.find? (fun c => decide (c.ask = a)) cs) with | some c_1 => (some c_1.answer) | none => none)

remember = fun (a : Ask) (answer : Prop) => do
    modify (fun cs => (List.take (Int.toNat 1024) ((Cached.mk a answer) :: (List.filter (fun c => decide (¬(c.ask = a))) cs))))

vocabulary: allowed: the service's answer to a check at a version (whether it allows the request): whether the person has the relation on the object, by the tuples of that version
levels: the resolution depth, one entry per step a check may take (a userset, an implied relation or a link is a step), as configured: 25 entries in production, as OpenFGA's default
schema: the schema in force: for each kind of object, its relations and the rules that give each
writes: every write and delete of a tuple, in order: version v is what the first v of them leave
uses: case class Obj(kind: String, id: String)
case class Query(obj: Obj, rel: String, person: String)
enum Subject: case Person(id: String), case Members(obj: Obj, rel: String), case Link(obj: Obj)
case class RelTuple(obj: Obj, rel: String, subject: Subject)
enum Write: case Add(t: RelTuple), case Remove(t: RelTuple)
enum Rule: case Direct, case Implied(by: String), case Inherited(link: String, rel: String)
case class RelationDef(kind: String, rel: String, rules: List[Rule])
granted = (q: Term[Query], v: Term[Int]) => holds(levels, tuplesAt(writes, v), q.obj, q.rel, q.person)

holds = (fuel: Term[List[Unit]], ts: Term[List[RelTuple]], o: Term[Obj], r: Term[String], p: Term[String]) =>
    fuel.on[Nil.type](False).on[::[Unit]]((_, rest) =>
      rulesOf(o.kind, r).exists(rule =>
        rule.on[Rule.Direct.type](
              ts.exists(t => t.obj === o && t.rel === r && t.subject
                .on[Subject.Person](id => id === p)
                .on[Subject.Members]((g, gr) => holds(rest, ts, g, gr, p))
                .on[Subject.Link](_ => False)))
            .on[Rule.Implied](by => holds(rest, ts, o, by, p))
            .on[Rule.Inherited]((link, via) =>
              ts.exists(t => t.obj === o && t.rel === link && t.subject
                .on[Subject.Person](_ => False)
                .on[Subject.Members]((_, _) => False)
                .on[Subject.Link](parent => holds(rest, ts, parent, via, p))))))

rulesOf = (kind: Term[String], rel: Term[String]) =>
  schema.find(d => d.kind === kind && d.rel === rel).on[Some[RelationDef]](d => d.rules).on[None.type](Nil)

tuplesAt = (ws: Term[List[Write]], v: Term[Int]) =>
  ws.take(v).foldLeft(Nil: Term[List[RelTuple]])((ts, w) => applyWrite(ts, w))

applyWrite = (ts: Term[List[RelTuple]], w: Term[Write]) =>
  w.on[Write.Add](t => If(ts.contains(t))(ts).Else(ts ++ List(t)))
   .on[Write.Remove](t => ts.filterNot(x => x === t))

val checkContract = Node.contract(allowed)("CheckContract",
  "A check at a version answers yes exactly when the tuples of that version give the person the relation under the schema, within the depth.",
  why = "The two halves, for one call, so every answer the running service gives is checked. The service resolves through the store's index and the schema index (StoreIndex, SchemaIndex); Lean proves that resolution gives what the tuples of the version give.",
  idea = "Checks"
)((q, v, answer) => answer === granted(q, v))
  .under(onlyGivenAccess, givenAccessAnswered)
  .examples(schema.bind(demoSchema), levels.bind(demoLevels), writes.bind(demoWrites))(
    expect(Query(readme, "viewer", "ann"), 3, true, "at version 3 ann is in the eng group, whose members view the folder that holds the readme"),
    expect(Query(readme, "viewer", "ann"), 2, false, "at version 2 ann is not yet in the group"),
    expect(Query(readme, "viewer", "ann"), 5, false, "at version 5 she has left the group: the later write takes her access away"),
    expect(Query(readme, "viewer", "bob"), 4, true, "bob edits the readme, and an editor is a viewer"),
    reject(Query(readme, "editor", "ann"), 3, true, "viewing never implies editing"),
    reject(Query(readme, "viewer", "ann"), 3, false, "a derivation through a group and a folder is not turned away"))

content.idea:
## Checks


A check names an object, a relation and a person, and the version it reads.
Tuples say who has which relation on which object: `doc:readme#viewer@user:ann`.
Groups and folders nest, so a check may follow several steps; it follows at most
the configured resolution depth (25 steps by default, as OpenFGA), and what is
given only in more steps is answered no. The service also writes and deletes
tuples.

sources.formula: forall((q: Term[Query], v: Term[Int]) => granted(q, v) ==> allowed(q, v))

vocabulary: allowed: the service's answer to a check at a version (whether it allows the request): whether the person has the relation on the object, by the tuples of that version
levels: the resolution depth, one entry per step a check may take (a userset, an implied relation or a link is a step), as configured: 25 entries in production, as OpenFGA's default
schema: the schema in force: for each kind of object, its relations and the rules that give each
writes: every write and delete of a tuple, in order: version v is what the first v of them leave
uses: case class Obj(kind: String, id: String)
case class Query(obj: Obj, rel: String, person: String)
enum Subject: case Person(id: String), case Members(obj: Obj, rel: String), case Link(obj: Obj)
case class RelTuple(obj: Obj, rel: String, subject: Subject)
enum Write: case Add(t: RelTuple), case Remove(t: RelTuple)
enum Rule: case Direct, case Implied(by: String), case Inherited(link: String, rel: String)
case class RelationDef(kind: String, rel: String, rules: List[Rule])
granted = (q: Term[Query], v: Term[Int]) => holds(levels, tuplesAt(writes, v), q.obj, q.rel, q.person)

holds = (fuel: Term[List[Unit]], ts: Term[List[RelTuple]], o: Term[Obj], r: Term[String], p: Term[String]) =>
    fuel.on[Nil.type](False).on[::[Unit]]((_, rest) =>
      rulesOf(o.kind, r).exists(rule =>
        rule.on[Rule.Direct.type](
              ts.exists(t => t.obj === o && t.rel === r && t.subject
                .on[Subject.Person](id => id === p)
                .on[Subject.Members]((g, gr) => holds(rest, ts, g, gr, p))
                .on[Subject.Link](_ => False)))
            .on[Rule.Implied](by => holds(rest, ts, o, by, p))
            .on[Rule.Inherited]((link, via) =>
              ts.exists(t => t.obj === o && t.rel === link && t.subject
                .on[Subject.Person](_ => False)
                .on[Subject.Members]((_, _) => False)
                .on[Subject.Link](parent => holds(rest, ts, parent, via, p))))))

rulesOf = (kind: Term[String], rel: Term[String]) =>
  schema.find(d => d.kind === kind && d.rel === rel).on[Some[RelationDef]](d => d.rules).on[None.type](Nil)

tuplesAt = (ws: Term[List[Write]], v: Term[Int]) =>
  ws.take(v).foldLeft(Nil: Term[List[RelTuple]])((ts, w) => applyWrite(ts, w))

applyWrite = (ts: Term[List[RelTuple]], w: Term[Write]) =>
  w.on[Write.Add](t => If(ts.contains(t))(ts).Else(ts ++ List(t)))
   .on[Write.Remove](t => ts.filterNot(x => x === t))

## The schema


For each kind of object, the schema names its relations and the rules that give
each: the relation's own tuples; a userset as the subject of a tuple
(`group:eng#member`: everyone who is a member of the group); a relation implied
by another on the same object (an editor is a viewer); and a relation inherited
through a link (a document's viewers include the viewers of its parent folder).

content.idea:
# Relationship-based access

A service that answers whether a person may do something to an object, from
relationship tuples and a schema, in the style of Google Zanzibar and OpenFGA.
A check of whether a person has a relation to an object, at a version, answers
yes exactly when the tuples stored at that version give it under the schema,
within the resolution depth.

## Checks

From: Q1, Q3

A check names an object, a relation and a person, and the version it reads.
Tuples say who has which relation on which object: `doc:readme#viewer@user:ann`.
Groups and folders nest, so a check may follow several steps; it follows at most
the configured resolution depth (25 steps by default, as OpenFGA), and what is
given only in more steps is answered no. The service also writes and deletes
tuples.

## The schema

From: Q2

For each kind of object, the schema names its relations and the rules that give
each: the relation's own tuples; a userset as the subject of a tuple
(`group:eng#member`: everyone who is a member of the group); a relation implied
by another on the same object (an editor is a viewer); and a relation inherited
through a link (a document's viewers include the viewers of its parent folder).

## Versions and the cache

From: Q4

Each write and delete gets the next version. A check answers from the tuples
the writes up to its version leave, never from another version's. A cache may
answer checks it has answered before, but never with an answer of another
version.

## Not modelled

From: Q5

Schema changes over time (the schema is fixed); exclusion, intersection and
conditions; who may write tuples; listing the users of an object; a watch API;
replication across regions.

content.statement: The schema index gives a relation of a kind of object exactly the rules the schema gives it, and none for a relation the schema does not name.
content.why: Checks look rules up on every step; an index by kind and relation makes that cheap. Lean proves `rulesOf` meets this contract; the index that runs (SchemaIndex.scala, plain Scala) is checked against `rulesOf` on the examples and on generated schemas. The check is proven from the contract.
examples: expect ("doc", "viewer") ⇒ List(Direct, Implied("editor"), Inherited("parent", "viewer"))  given schema = List(RelationDef("doc", "viewer", List(Direct, Implied("editor"), Inherited("parent", "viewer"))), RelationDef("doc", "editor", List(Direct)), RelationDef("folder", "viewer", List(Direct)), RelationDef("group", "member", List(Direct)))  — a document's viewers: its own tuples, its editors, and its folder's viewers

reject ("folder", "viewer") ⇒ List(Direct, Implied("editor"))  given schema = List(RelationDef("doc", "viewer", List(Direct, Implied("editor"), Inherited("parent", "viewer"))), RelationDef("doc", "editor", List(Direct)), RelationDef("folder", "viewer", List(Direct)), RelationDef("group", "member", List(Direct)))  — a rule the schema does not give a relation is never added

content.statement: One process holds the tuple store and the cache; a write is applied under a lock and gets the next version; a check runs CachedChecks' flow at the version it names, or the latest, through the cache.
content.why: What a check answers is proven (CheckContract, CachedChecks); that writes are serialised, that a check reads one version, and how requests are parsed are decided here and reviewed. Tuple strings are parsed by plain code (RebacService.parse): a malformed one is refused with a 400, so it can never become a tuple.

content.statement: A read of an object's tuples at a version returns exactly the tuples about that object that the writes up to that version leave, in the order they were added.
content.why: The tuples live in the store, which keeps them by object and version; the check is proven from this promise, not from the store's code. The in-memory store (TupleStore) stands for a database here: its reads are checked against `storedOf` (this promise as code) on the examples and on generated logs of writes, not proven.

val storeIndex = Node.assumption(tuplesOf)("StoreIndex",
  "A read of an object's tuples at a version returns exactly the tuples about that object that the writes up to that version leave, in the order they were added.",
  why = "The tuples live in the store, which keeps them by object and version; the check is proven from this promise, not from the store's code.   idea = "Versions and the cache"
